skill.name: database-migrations-migration-observability
skill.description: Build observability for database migrations with CDC metrics, dashboards, anomaly detection, and alerts.
skill.summary: Guides migration monitoring with CDC pipelines, Prometheus metrics, Grafana dashboards, and alerting workflows.
skill.author: sickn33

security_audit.summary: The static findings are false positives in documentation examples: markdown code fences, JavaScript template literals, configured network calls, and migration configuration values. No evidence found of prompt injection, hardcoded exfiltration endpoints, credential harvesting, or self-executing commands in SKILL.md. The examples still need normal review before users copy them into production automation.

remediation.issue: Network examples use configured service URLs and webhooks.
remediation.suggestion: Document that users must review endpoints, tokens, and payload contents before enabling Kafka Connect, Grafana, or Slack requests.

remediation.issue: CI examples include runnable migration monitoring commands.
remediation.suggestion: Add a note to test commands in staging and require approval before production migration workflows run automatically.

remediation.issue: Dashboard and alert examples rely on service credentials.
remediation.suggestion: Recommend least-privilege tokens, secret storage, and log redaction for Grafana tokens and Slack webhooks.

content.value_statement: Database migrations can fail silently when lag, errors, and throughput are invisible. This skill guides CDC metrics, dashboards, alerts, and health checks for safer migration work.
actual_capabilities: Designs observable MongoDB migration flows with counters, histograms, and error metrics.
Outlines CDC pipelines with Debezium, Kafka consumers, and replication lag tracking.
Defines Prometheus metrics for duration, rows migrated, data lag, and error rates.
Creates alerting patterns for Slack, email, and severity-based migration events.
Provides Grafana dashboard panel examples for progress, lag, and migration errors.
Shows CI workflow structure for starting monitoring, running migrations, and checking health.
limitations: It provides implementation patterns, not a complete tested migration product.
Examples need adaptation for each database, network, and security model.
It does not verify credentials, schemas, or connector compatibility automatically.
It cannot replace production load testing or disaster recovery planning.

use_cases.title: Plan migration observability
use_cases.description: Create metrics, dashboards, and alert paths before a high-risk database migration begins.

use_cases.title: Monitor CDC pipelines
use_cases.description: Track Debezium and Kafka event flow while source and target databases stay synchronized.

use_cases.title: Review rollout health
use_cases.description: Define CI checks that validate migration lag, throughput, and failure signals after deployment.

prompt_templates.title: Start a monitoring plan
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a single migration.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a migration observability plan for my database move. Include core metrics, dashboard sections, alert thresholds, and health checks.

prompt_templates.title: Design CDC monitoring
prompt_templates.prompt: Design CDC monitoring for a Debezium and Kafka migration. Include consumer lag, replication lag, error metrics, and alert routing.

prompt_templates.title: Build dashboard coverage
prompt_templates.prompt: Map my migration stages to Prometheus metrics and Grafana panels. Cover progress, lag, throughput, errors, and rollback readiness.

prompt_templates.title: Audit production readiness
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this migration observability design for production readiness. Identify missing alerts, unsafe assumptions, monitoring gaps, and operational runbooks.

output_examples.input: Plan observability for a PostgreSQL to MongoDB migration with CDC.
output: Metric plan covering migration duration, documents processed, replication lag, and error rate.
Dashboard layout for progress, data lag, throughput, and failed operations.
Alert policy for high lag, low throughput, failed connector tasks, and rollback triggers.

output_examples.input: Create checks for a CI migration workflow.
output: Pre-run checklist for credentials, connector status, and baseline lag.
Runtime checks for monitoring startup, migration execution, and maximum lag.
Post-run review for alert history, migrated row counts, and dashboard evidence.

output_examples.input: Review alerting for a migration dashboard.
output_examples.output: The review identifies missing replication lag alerts, weak error-rate thresholds, and missing ownership for critical Slack notifications.

best_practices: Define migration success, lag, and rollback thresholds before writing automation.
Test dashboards and alerts in staging with realistic data volume.
Store service tokens in secret managers and redact them from logs.
anti_patterns: Running production migrations before metrics and alerts are visible.
Using one generic alert for every migration failure mode.
Copying webhook or dashboard examples without reviewing endpoint security.

faq.question: Does this skill run migrations for me?
faq.answer: No. It guides observability design and example implementation for migration monitoring.

faq.question: Can it support both SQL and NoSQL migrations?
faq.answer: Yes. The guidance covers database migration monitoring patterns that can be adapted to both styles.

faq.question: Does it require Debezium?
faq.answer: No. Debezium is one example for CDC, but the monitoring concepts can apply to other CDC tools.

faq.question: Can I use it with Claude, Codex, or Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The skill metadata declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Will it create production-ready dashboards automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides dashboard structures and prompts that need environment-specific validation.

faq.question: How should I handle credentials in the examples?
faq.answer: Use secret storage, least-privilege tokens, and redacted logs for Grafana, Kafka, database, and Slack credentials.
